difficulty_reason: Several configuration surfaces (app versions with URLs and scopes, compliance webhooks, listing content, a 1200x1200 icon spec, contact details) but no individually hard step, and Shopify's CLI/templates handle the token flow for you. Rating configuration complexity only; the public App Store review burden is rated separately under approval.
setup_time: ~30 minutes to a working development-store install

approval.kind: Shopify App Store review, required only for PUBLIC distribution (listed or unlisted); development-store installs and single-merchant custom apps need no review
approval.wait: no committed timeline from Shopify; the submission-confirmation email has cited 'up to 2 weeks', while Shopify staff decline to give timeframes and community reports run 2-6+ weeks during submission-volume spikes
approval.notes: Review is triggered only by choosing public distribution - even an unlisted public app must pass review before multiple merchants can install it. Statuses flow Draft -> Submitted -> (Paused if core requirements fail) -> Reviewed -> Published, with email at each transition. Repeat failed exchanges trigger escalating cooldown periods. Two submission limits apply: only one new app per organization in review at a time, and organizations with published apps need 10+ paid installs on each before submitting another new app. Access to protected customer data is a SEPARATE approval that cannot be requested while the app is under review.
approval.wait_short: none for dev stores; weeks for public

summary: The friendliest split in this library: building and installing on development stores is fully self-serve (~30 minutes, no review), and Shopify's CLI and app templates handle the OAuth token flow for you. The gate appears only when you want public distribution - then a human App Store review applies, with automated pre-checks, an AI self-review tool, email-driven fix cycles, escalating cooldowns for repeat failures, and no committed timeline. Plan the review, not the setup, if you are heading to the App Store.

steps.title: Create a Partner account and open the Dev Dashboard
steps.detail: Sign up free at shopify.com/partners. All app management - creation, versions, installs, review - happens in the Dev Dashboard. You need a user with app development permissions.

steps.title: Create the app
steps.detail: In the Dev Dashboard: Apps -> Create app -> Start from Dev Dashboard, name it, Create. Note Shopify's own steer: apps headed for the App Store should be built with Shopify CLI instead, which scaffolds the project and wires up Shopify managed installation.

steps.title: Release a version with URLs and scopes
steps.detail: A version is a snapshot of your app's configuration; the app needs at least one released version before it can be installed anywhere. Set the App URL, webhooks API version, and access scopes. Scopes touching protected customer data require a separate approval.

steps.title: Install on a development store and test the OAuth grant
steps.detail: Create a development store, then from the app's overview page click Install app and pick the store. You should land on the OAuth grant screen - if you don't, your App URL or redirect URLs are wrong, and Shopify will not approve the app later until that flow works. CLI-built apps get Shopify managed installation and skip this failure mode.

steps.title: Authenticate API calls - don't hand-roll OAuth
steps.detail: Shopify is explicit: most apps should not implement the token flow by hand. Shopify CLI and the official app templates handle authentication for the GraphQL Admin API; other Shopify APIs issue their own token types.

steps.title: Complete the App Store review page (public distribution only)
steps.detail: Set URLs (no 'Shopify' in domains or contact emails), subscribe to compliance webhooks, upload a 1200x1200 JPEG/PNG icon, provide API and emergency contacts, and create at least one listing with a primary language. Then run the automated checks and the AI self-review against your codebase - both must pass before submission.

steps.title: Submit and work the review
steps.detail: Submit from the App Store review page. Watch the status banner: Paused means fix core issues and Submit fixes; Reviewed means your reviewer needs answers - reply to their email to continue. Address EVERY piece of feedback in one resubmit; repeated partial fixes trigger escalating cooldowns.

requirements: A free Shopify Partner account with app development permissions
Hosting for your App URL and redirect URLs
A scopes decision (protected customer data needs separate approval)
For public distribution: listing content, 1200x1200 icon, compliance webhook subscriptions, emergency contact, and a working OAuth install flow
nuances: Review applies to public distribution only - but 'unlisted' public apps are NOT exempt: any app installed by multiple merchants must pass review.
Single-merchant custom apps and development-store installs skip review entirely.
Shopify staff decline to commit to review timelines; the submission-confirmation email has cited 'up to 2 weeks', and community reports run 2-6+ weeks during volume spikes.
Submission limits: one new app per organization in review at a time, and every published app needs 10+ paid installs before you can submit another new one (install counts refresh once a day).
Protected customer data approval is a separate track and CANNOT be requested while the app is under review - sequence it before submitting.
Repeat failed review exchanges trigger cooldowns that get longer each time; during a cooldown the app is Paused and cannot be resubmitted until the date in the status banner.
App icon must be exactly 1200x1200 pixels, JPEG or PNG; 'Shopify' (or misspellings of it) is banned from your domains and contact emails.
The AI self-review only covers requirements checkable from your codebase; listing content, live behavior and UX are still verified by humans after submission.

common_blockers.problem: Installing on the dev store never shows the OAuth grant screen.
common_blockers.solution: Your App URL or allowed redirect URLs are misconfigured. Fix them and retest - or use Shopify CLI's managed installation, which handles this automatically. An app whose install flow doesn't reach the grant screen will not be approved.

common_blockers.problem: App stuck in Paused or bouncing between submissions.
common_blockers.solution: Address every reviewer point in a single resubmit (use the per-requirement responses on the review page) and pass the automated checks + AI self-review before resubmitting. Partial fixes are what trigger escalating cooldowns.

common_blockers.problem: Can't submit a second app: status shows Submission limited.
common_blockers.solution: Either your organization already has a new app in review (wait for publication or cooldown, or withdraw it if it's still waiting on a reviewer), or a published app has fewer than 10 paid installs - hit that threshold first; counts update once a day.

agent_can_do: Scaffold the app with Shopify CLI and wire authentication via the official templates
Run the automated checks and AI self-review, then fix what they flag
Draft the listing content, testing instructions and reviewer credentials package
Advise on scope selection and whether protected customer data is really needed
human_must_do: Create the Partner account and the app in the Dev Dashboard
Submit the app for review and reply to reviewer emails
Provide test-store credentials for the reviewer
Request protected customer data access if the app needs it

evidence.claim: Apps are created free in the Dev Dashboard (Apps -> Create app); a released version (App URL, webhooks API version, scopes) is required before any installation; development-store installs are self-serve via the Install app button.

Public app review flows Draft -> Submitted -> (Paused for core-requirement failures, resumable via Submit fixes) -> Reviewed (reviewer dialogue by email) -> Published; withdrawal is possible while waiting on a reviewer.

Public submissions require compliance webhook subscriptions, a 1200x1200 icon, API and emergency contacts, a listing with a primary language, and passing automated checks; submission limits (one new app in review per organization; 10+ paid installs on each published app) and escalating cooldowns for repeat failures are documented.

Before submitting, the app must be production-ready, tested on a development store, and its App URL/redirects must reach the OAuth grant screen; an AI self-review tool checks code-evaluable requirements pre-submission.
Shopify explicitly says most apps should not implement OAuth by hand - the CLI and app templates handle the token flow for the GraphQL Admin API.

Shopify commits to no review timeframe: staff state they cannot provide estimates during high submission volume, the confirmation email has cited 'up to 2 weeks', and community reports run 2-6+ weeks; even unlisted public apps require review before multi-merchant installation.
The Partner entry point at https://www.shopify.com/partners responds (HTTP 200); account creation requires a human signup.

uncertainties: Actual review duration is volatile and volume-dependent - anywhere from days to 6+ weeks in recent community reports; there is no SLA.
The AI self-review tool is new and covers only code-checkable requirements; its effect on real review times is unproven.
Listing visibility tiers (fully visible vs limited) and App Store content requirements change over time.
